questions.solution: The electronegativity order of hybridized carbons is $sp > sp^{2} > sp^{3}$. So in an allylic halide, such as $C{H}_{2} = CH - C{H}_{2} - I$ , the alpha carbon is much more partially positive than the alpha carbon in $C{H}_{3} - C{H}_{2} - C{H}_{2}I$. Therefore, the attacking nucleophile will be attracted to the alpha carbon more in the allylic halide compound than in the primary halide. Hence, allylic halides tend to follow ${S}_{N} \text{2}$ pathways more than primary halides.

questions.explanation:
Boiling point of the given compounds decreases in the following order as when molecular weight decreases magnitude of Van der Waal's forces also decreases so boiling point also decreases.
$C{H}_{3}C{H}_{2}C{H}_{2}C{H}_{2}Cl > C{H}_{3}C{H}_{2}C{H}_{2}Cl > C{H}_{3}C{H}_{2}Cl > C{H}_{3}Cl$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The alcoholic solution of $KOH$ is used in which type of the organic reactions?
questions.solution:
$C{H}_{3}C{H}_{2}Br + alcKOH\overset{dehydrohalogenation}{→}C{H}_{2} = C{H}_{2} + KBr + {H}_{2}O$

In alcoholic KOH alkoxide ions $\left(RO^{-}\right)$ are present which is a strong base. They abstract proton from beta carbon of alkyl halide and favours elimination reaction

$ROH + KOH \to ROK + {H}_{2}O$

$ROK \to RO^{-} + K^{+}$

$RO^{-} + H - \overset{β}{C{H}_{2}} - \overset{α}{C{H}_{2}} - Br \to ROH + C{H}_{2} = C{H}_{2} + Br^{-}$
